newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to focus on corruption in address -agency.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to focus on corruption in address -agency.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will announce urgent measures to weed out corruption in his planned address to parliament next month, Interfax news agency said on Saturday.

"The president's address will include special measures on the decriminalisation of economic life and the suppression of the basic conditions that feed corruption," Interfax said, quoting unnamed sources in Yeltsin's circle.
Yeltsin, who is still recovering from pneumonia at a state residence outside Moscow, is expected to make his annual address to both houses of parliament on March 6.
The president will demand that all channels of state spending be brought under tighter control and that their property and powers be more clearly defined, Interfax said.
Yeltsin envisages a stronger role for the tax police and for the Federal Security Service (successor to the Soviet-era KGB) in the fight against economic crime, it said.
Any officials demonstrating "excessive wealth" will be subject to more thorough and severe checks.
Earlier this week Yeltsin gave Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov "carte blanche" to crack down on economic crimes, which cost Russia's state coffers billions of dollars every year.
The government often blames tax dodgers -- companies and individuals -- for chronic delays in paying wages and pensions.

Yeltsin had originally been due to make his address this month but it was postponed because of his poor health. Yeltsin, 66, went down with pneumonia on January 8, just two weeks after returning from the Kremlin after recovering from heart surgery.

On Saturday Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, who has in the past urged Yeltsin to retire on health grounds, told Interfax he hoped Yeltsin would give a "real assessment of the situation in the country and of his personal possibilities" in his address to parliament.
